confirmed.title: Privacy policy promises IP/device counters are kept at most two days, but the storage code keeps them up to about four
confirmed.description: The counters now live in the QuotaCounter Durable Object (server/yerim-ai/src/store.ts), not in KV. storageKV gives each value an expiry, but an expired value is only removed when it is read again or when the daily alarm sweep runs (DAY_MS). Each put also sets the expiry again to now + 48 h, so a daily key such as `ip:<day>:<IP>` or `q:<day>:<deviceId>` lives until 48 h after its last write in that day. Expired entries can then sit in storage for up to another 24 h before the sweep deletes them. The public privacy policy and both READMEs give 'at most two days' as a fixed limit, and the server README still says the counters are in KV.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A device makes its first AI call at 00:05 Istanbul time and its last at 23:55. The key `ip:2026-10-17:<IP>` gets expiry 2026-10-19 23:55. Nobody reads it again, so it is removed only by the next alarm sweep, which can run up to 24 h later (about 2026-10-20 23:55). The IP address then sits in storage for almost four days after it was first recorded. The App Store privacy text ('at most two days') is therefore false.
confirmed.evidence: server/yerim-ai/src/store.ts:186-189 `const ttl = opts?.expirationTtl ?? DEFAULT_TTL_SECONDS; await storage.put(key, { v: value, e: clock() + ttl * 1000 } ...); ... setAlarm(clock() + DAY_MS)`; store.ts:254-257 `async alarm() { await this.queue(() => this.kv.sweep()); await this.storage.setAlarm(Date.now() + DAY_MS); }`; quota.ts:106-108 ipGuard puts the key again with `expirationTtl: TTL_SECONDS` (172800) on every call; docs/gizlilik.html:49 "IP adresine bağlı sayaçlar en fazla iki gün tutulur" (and :95 in English); README.md:117; server/yerim-ai/README.md:41 "Hak sayaçları ... KV'de en fazla iki gün tutulur."

votes.reason:
I traced the code and the finding holds. In server/yerim-ai/src/store.ts, storageKV.put stores each value with an expiry of `e: clock() + ttl*1000`, and ttl defaults to 172800 s. An expired value is removed only in two places: when get() reads it, or when sweep() runs from QuotaCounter.alarm(). That alarm runs once a day: it is first set to clock()+DAY_MS and then re-set to Date.now()+DAY_MS after each sweep.

In quota.ts, ipGuard (line 108) writes `ip:${todayIstanbul(now)}:${ip}` again on every call with expirationTtl 172800. charge (line 68) does the same for `q:<day>:<deviceId>`. Every write moves the expiry to 48 h after that write. The key is a day key, and no one reads it after that Istanbul day ends. The one exception is peek/refund on the same day key, which only happens within that day.

So the key lives until 48 h after its last write in the day, plus up to 24 h of sweep delay. Examples:
- A single write at 00:05 is removed between 48 h and about 72 h later.
- A first write at 00:05 and a last write at 23:55 can stay in storage until about 4 days after the first write.

The stored key holds the raw IP address. index.ts:196 passes the CF-Connecting-IP value straight in, and lines 132 and 154 add `quota:`/`cancel:` prefixes but still store the raw IP.

The documents promise otherwise:
- docs/gizlilik.html:49 says "en fazla iki gün tutulur" ("kept at most two days"), and the English version says "kept for at most two days".
- README.md says "en fazla iki gün tutar".
- server/yerim-ai/README.md still says the counters are stored "KV'de" (in KV), although they are now in the Durable Object.

This is a real gap between the public privacy policy and the code for personal data (IP addresses). It does not crash anything or break a feature, so I rate it medium as a compliance and accuracy issue.

I could not refute this. Every AI request reaches the code path. wrangler.toml binds the QUOTA_DO Durable Object (class QuotaCounter, lines 16-22), and index.ts:54 selects objectQuota(env.QUOTA_DO) whenever that binding is present, so the deployed counters live in Durable Object storage through storageKV, not in Workers KV. Every call refreshes the expiry: ipGuard (quota.ts:103-108, called from index.ts:196 with the raw client IP and from :134/:154 with 'quota:'/'cancel:' prefixes) does a put on each call, and so does charge (quota.ts:65), each time with expirationTtl 172800. In storageKV.put (store.ts:197-198) that sets e = now + 48h. A daily key such as ip:<day>:<IP> therefore expires 48 h after the last write of that day, which can be about 72 h after the first write. An expired value is only removed when get reads it again (store.ts:188-191) or when the alarm sweep runs. The sweep is scheduled once per DAY_MS (store.ts:201, :254-257), so an expired value can stay up to about 24 h more. Past days' keys are never read again, because each key holds the date. In the worst case the raw IP address and device ID stay stored for close to 4 days. The policy says "en fazla iki gün" / "at most two days" (docs/gizlilik.html:49 and :95, README.md:117, server/yerim-ai/README.md:41), and the server README still names KV as the store. This is a real mismatch between the public privacy policy / App Store disclosure and how long the data is actually kept. The data is small (a counter keyed by IP or device ID) and the fix is easy (a shorter TTL, sweeping more often, or changing the wording), so I rate it medium rather than high.

I confirmed this from the code. The finding is real, but its severity is lower than claimed.

How a counter is stored and removed:
- In `server/yerim-ai/src/quota.ts:102-108`, `ipGuard` keeps the raw IP in the key `ip:${todayIstanbul(now)}:${ip}`. Every call writes it again with `expirationTtl: TTL_SECONDS` (172800 s = 48 h). The `q:` device keys at lines 68 and 87 work the same way.
- In `server/yerim-ai/src/store.ts:196-198`, `storageKV.put` sets the expiry to `clock() + ttl*1000` on each write. The 48 h therefore counts from the last write of that Istanbul day, not the first.
- An expired value is deleted only when it is read (`get`, lines 187-193) or when the alarm sweep runs.
- The sweep runs once a day: the alarm is set to `clock() + DAY_MS` (line 201) and re-armed in `alarm()` with `Date.now() + DAY_MS` (lines 254-257).
- A past day's key is never read again, because `ipGuard` and `peek` only read today's key. Old keys therefore wait for the sweep.

How long an IP can stay stored:
- First write at 00:05, last write at 23:55: the expiry is about 2 days from the last write, which is about 3 days after the IP was first recorded.
- The sweep can then come up to 24 h after expiry, for roughly 4 days in total.
- Even with no sweep delay, the TTL reset alone breaks a fixed two-day limit.

What the documents say:
- `docs/gizlilik.html:49` and `:95`, `README.md` (Gizlilik section) and `server/yerim-ai/README.md:41` all state "en fazla iki gün" / "at most two days". The last one also still says "KV".
- Nothing in the code comments or tests describes the limit any other way.
- Commit d1c66f7 only brought the docs up to date. It did not change retention.

So the public privacy statement about how long a raw IP is kept is false.

Why low rather than medium:
- The data is a small counter keyed by IP and device ID. It is never exposed and is deleted automatically.
- The gap is one to two extra days.
- The fix is to correct the wording, or to shorten the TTL and sweep more often.

It is a real accuracy problem in a privacy disclosure, but the user harm is limited.

confirmed.title: English follow-up and example chips are Turkish-only phrases in disguise: on the rule path every one of them misfires
confirmed.description: suggestions() is documented as "Follow-up phrases the assistant already understands (see detectFollowUp)". detectFollowUp (assistant.ts:517) only recognises Turkish: `/\bdaha yakin\w*/`, `otopark ... ucretsiz`, `baska` plus WIDER_WORDS, and `bir de X ... bak`. The English strings in en.ts (sugNearer 'closer', sugFreePark 'with free parking', sugOther 'anything else?', sugElsewhere 'try {{d}} too') match none of these. The example chips have the same problem: exAlsancak 'Car park in {{a}}', exNear 'Car park near me', exStadium 'Stadium car park', exKofte 'Meatballs near me' and exBreakfast 'Breakfast in {{a}}' are sent as messages, but the rule parser has no English filler words ('car', 'in', 'near', 'me'). So the chip phrase list and the detector disagree whenever the UI is in English. The rule path is what answers whenever the AI is off, the 10 daily uses are gone, or the router times out or fails.
confirmed.failure_scenario: Reproduced with jest on the real assistant and the real i18n, AI off. After 'alsancak köfte' returns 5 cards, the English chips give: 'closer' -> "Is \"closer\" a dish or a place? I'm not sure." (0 cards; Turkish 'daha yakın' re-sorts by distance). 'with free parking' -> same 'dish or place?' reply. 'anything else?' -> same. 'try Karşıyaka too' -> "I couldn't find a place or dish called \"try too\" in Karşıyaka." Example chips from a fresh context: 'Car park near me' -> "I couldn't find a place called \"car near me\"". 'Stadium car park' -> "...called \"stadium car\"". 'Car park in Alsancak' -> "...called \"car in alsancak\"". 'Meatballs near me' -> 'dish or place?'. 'Breakfast in Alsancak' -> a single restaurant whose name contains "in alsancak". The Turkish versions of the same chips all return 5 correct cards.
confirmed.evidence: src/components/chat/model.ts:185-196 `/** Follow-up phrases the assistant already understands (see detectFollowUp). */ export function suggestions(...) { ... out.push(t('chat.sugNearer')); ... }`. src/i18n/en.ts:584-588 `sugNearer: 'closer', sugFreePark: 'with free parking', sugOther: 'anything else?', sugElsewhere_0: 'try {{d}} too'`. src/i18n/en.ts:727-733 `exAlsancak: 'Car park in {{a}}', exNear: 'Car park near me', exStadium: 'Stadium car park', exKofte: 'Meatballs near me', exBreakfast: 'Breakfast in {{a}}'`. src/data/assistant.ts:523-535 detectFollowUp matches only `otopark\w*\s+ucretsiz`, `daha yakin`, `baska` and `bir de ... bak`. Chips are sent as messages in src/app/sohbet.tsx:394-395 `suggestions={picks} onPick={(text) => void send(text)}`.

confirmed.title: Leftover 'gibberish never reaches the AI' guard now throws away the router's answer after the use is already charged
confirmed.description: Commit 4bbff78 added the gibberish kind so that 'Oo' or 'hmm' would get an 'anlamadım' reply with no ✨ spent. Later, 74ebf92 made route() call Haiku first for every message (line 984, before any rule check). The old guard was left in two places. Line 1082 skips the AI's search when parseQuery says gibberish, and line 1151 still claims gibberish 'never reaches the AI above'. scripts/ai-eval.ts:82 repeats the same false claim ('the app catches gibberish before the AI anyway'). isGibberish (intent.ts:425-430) marks any text with no vowel as gibberish unless it is a single word that matches a place name word, so real requests count as gibberish. The Worker keeps the use for any 200 /understand answer, so the user pays for an AI reading that the app then ignores.
confirmed.failure_scenario: AI on, İzmir. The user types 'KFC nerede' or 'kfc yakınımda' (there are several restaurants named 'KFC' in the data). parseQuery returns {kind:'gibberish'} for both, as does plain 'KFC' (checked with tsx). route() has already sent the text to /understand, and the Worker returns search {place/appleQuery:'KFC', food:true} and keeps one of the 10 daily uses. At line 1082 `it.kind !== 'gibberish'` is false, so the AI's reading is dropped. Line 1152 then answers 'chat.unknown' ('anlamadım') with no results. The same happens for 'BBQ', 'MCD' and similar no-vowel brand names.
confirmed.evidence: assistant.ts:984 `const routed = await route(text, ctx, deps);` runs unconditionally. assistant.ts:1082 `if (routed.out.kind === 'search' && !followUp && it.kind !== 'abuse' && it.kind !== 'gibberish') {`. assistant.ts:1151 `// 'gibberish' (too short / no vowel) never reaches the AI above: ask again, no search.` The 4bbff78 message said 'They are now gibberish: an "anlamadım" reply, no search, no ✨ spent'. intent.ts:430 `return !/[aeiou]/.test(letters) && !(text.indexOf(' ') < 0 && equalsNameWord(text));`. index.ts /understand always returns `respond('ok', { understanding, remaining: q.remaining })`, so the use is kept. A tsx run gave parseQuery('KFC nerede') = {kind:'gibberish'}, and allRestaurants() includes several entries named 'KFC'.

votes.reason: I traced it and ran it, and the finding holds. route() (assistant.ts:909-950) calls ai.understand for every message as long as uses are left, before parseQuery runs. parseQuery returns {kind:'gibberish'} for 'KFC nerede', 'kfc yakınımda', 'KFC', 'BBQ' and 'MCD' (checked with tsx). The cause is intent.ts:688 `if (!cat && !food && !hasPark && isGibberish(rest.join(' ')))`: the check runs on what is left after words like 'nerede' are removed, and 'kfc' has no vowel and is not a place name word. The guard at assistant.ts:1082 (`it.kind !== 'gibberish'`) then drops the router's search, and line 1152 answers chat.unknown. The comment at line 1151 ('never reaches the AI above') is false. End to end: I called answer() with a mock AI that returns search {place:'KFC', appleQuery:'KFC', food:true}. 'KFC nerede', 'KFC' and 'kfc yakınımda' each got chat.unknown with 0 cards, while 'Burger King nerede' got 5 cards. understand was called 4 times. KFC is in data/food-izmir.json and data/food-overture-izmir.json. On the server, index.ts:331 keeps the use on every ok /understand answer. The client only sends /cancel when a request times out (client.ts:214), so the ✨ use is spent and the user gets 'anlamadım'. Medium severity fits: a real user-facing failure for no-vowel brand names, plus a lost daily use.

I checked this against the code and could not refute it. Real users can reach it.

1. **The AI is always called first.** `route()` (src/data/assistant.ts:909-951) calls `ai.understand` for every new message whenever the AI is present and uses are left. Nothing checks for gibberish beforehand, and `answerText` calls it at line 984 before `parseQuery` ever runs.

2. **Real brand queries count as gibberish.** I ran `parseQuery` with bun from the scratchpad. 'KFC nerede', 'kfc yakınımda', 'KFC', 'kfc var mı', 'BBQ' and 'mcd' all return `{kind:'gibberish'}`. The cause is the check at intent.ts:688 (`isGibberish(rest.join(' '))`): once the filler words are gone, only 'kfc' is left, and it has no vowel. The fallback `equalsNameWord` does not rescue it, because it uses `searchPlaces`, which searches the landmark/place index. `searchPlaces('kfc')` returned []. Yet `allRestaurants()` holds about 25 entries named KFC, including 'Kfc Agora Avm İzmir'.

3. **The AI's answer is thrown away.** If the router returns search, line 1082 (`... && it.kind !== 'gibberish'`) skips `aiLedIntent`, so `meta.ai` stays null and `aiAdded` is false. The code then falls through to line 1152, which answers 'chat.unknown' with no cards. None of the earlier exits (greetKind, isReplyWord, followUp, which needs a previous ctx.place, routed 'unknown') saves it.

4. **The use is not given back.** The Worker returns `respond('ok', { understanding, remaining: q.remaining })` (index.ts:331). The client only calls /cancel on a timeout (client.ts:214), so the use stays spent.

Result: the user spends one of their ✨ uses, gets 'anlamadım' with no results, and the AI's correct reading is discarded. The comment at assistant.ts:1151 ("never reaches the AI above") is no longer true.

**Why medium:**
- Without AI the rule path fails the same way, so the extra harm from this bug is the charged use and the lost AI answer.
- It only hits no-vowel brand or abbreviation queries, but KFC is a common query.
- One thing I could not check without calling the API: whether Haiku actually returns search for 'KFC nerede'. It is plausible, and the drop happens whenever it does.

I confirmed this by running it. I put a throwaway jest test in the scratchpad (deleted afterwards), set the city to İzmir and mocked the AI so /understand returns search {place:'KFC', appleQuery:'KFC', food:true}. parseQuery gives {kind:'gibberish'} for 'KFC', 'KFC nerede', 'kfc yakınımda', 'BBQ' and 'MCD', and the İzmir data has 25 restaurants with KFC in the name. answer('KFC nerede') and answer('KFC') both returned chat.unknown ('anlamadım') with 0 cards, even though the mocked router had answered with a search.

Code path:
- route() at assistant.ts:984 calls ai.understand on every message.
- Line 1082 `it.kind !== 'gibberish'` drops the AI's search.
- Line 1152 returns chat.unknown.
- The Worker (index.ts:331) answers 'ok' with the remaining count. It only gives the use back on error or timeout, so this call costs one of the 10 daily uses.

Intent: the gibberish exclusion was a deliberate choice in 74ebf92 ('Follow-ups, abuse and gibberish stay with the rules'). It was meant to keep the AI from guessing on 'Oo' or 'hmm', so the guard as such is not a mistake. The defect is how the guard and isGibberish work together. isGibberish (intent.ts:425-430) is meant to let a short no-vowel name through when it is a real place (its own comment gives 'ptt'), but equalsNameWord only checks searchPlaces, not restaurant names. That makes real brand queries such as KFC count as gibberish, so the user gets 'anlamadım' instead of the 25 KFC results, and the AI use is still spent. No test checks that a no-vowel brand name should be gibberish. The intent.test cases are 'Oo', 'aa', 'xd', 'brb' and similar.

So this is a real wrong result on a common query, and it also costs the user a use. The stale comments (assistant.ts:1151, ai-eval.ts:82) are only a side point. Severity is medium: there is no crash and no data or security hole, but a well-known brand search fails and the paid use is wasted.

confirmed.title: Onboarding says location 'never leaves your device', but it is sent to Apple (rounded for car park search, exact for reverse geocoding)
confirmed.description: The onboarding location screen tells users 'Konumun cihazından çıkmaz' (EN src/i18n/en.ts:70: 'It never leaves your device'). This text dates from the first onboarding commit (df88863). Commit de49c72 later added Apple Maps car parks around the target, and since then the user's own GPS position leaves the phone: (a) sonuc.tsx 'Hemen bul' sets target = currentLocation(), and useRanked(target) -> useAppleParkings(target) -> YerimMapKit.searchParkingAsync(roundArea(target)) sends it to Apple, rounded to about 100 m; (b) konum-sec.tsx:79 calls lookup(loc) with the user's exact currentLocation, which runs Location.reverseGeocodeAsync (CLGeocoder, Apple servers) on the unrounded coordinates. The privacy section (tr.ts:329) does admit '~100 m' to Apple, so the app contradicts itself. That section also understates the exact-coordinate reverse geocode.
confirmed.failure_scenario: A user reads the onboarding promise, grants location and taps 'Hemen bul' or opens the pin picker. Their current position goes to Apple's MapKit search (rounded to about 100 m) and to Apple's reverse geocoder (exact). This contradicts the consent text shown when they granted the permission, a misleading privacy disclosure before App Store review.
confirmed.evidence: src/i18n/tr.ts:69 locBody: '...Konumun cihazından çıkmaz...'; src/i18n/en.ts:70 'It never leaves your device.'; src/data/appleParkings.ts:52 `YerimMapKit.searchParkingAsync(area.lat, area.lng, RADIUS_M)` with area = roundArea(target); src/app/sonuc.tsx: `const loc = await currentLocation(true, ...)` ... `setTarget(inside ? loc : city.center)` ... `useRanked(target)`; src/data/useParkings.ts:205 `const apple = useAppleParkings(target);`; src/app/konum-sec.tsx:79 `lookup(loc);` -> src/lib/location.ts:69 `Location.reverseGeocodeAsync({ latitude: loc.lat, longitude: loc.lng })`; src/i18n/tr.ts:329 '...yaklaşık bölgen (~100 m) Apple Haritalar'a gider...'

votes.reason:
I traced the code and the finding holds. The onboarding text in src/i18n/tr.ts:69 ("Konumun cihazından çıkmaz") and src/i18n/en.ts:70 ("It never leaves your device") promises the location stays on the phone.

The code sends it out in two places:

(a) Car park search. In src/app/sonuc.tsx:89-100, `loc = await currentLocation(true, ...)` and then `setTarget(inside ? loc : city.center)`. useRanked(target) is called at sonuc.tsx:111. src/data/useParkings.ts:205 calls `useAppleParkings(target)`, which rounds the target with roundArea (3 decimals, about 100 m). searchApple then calls `YerimMapKit.searchParkingAsync(area.lat, area.lng, RADIUS_M)`, an Apple MapKit search. So a rounded version of the user's GPS position goes to Apple.

Its storageKV only stamps an expiry on each value (2 days). An expired value is deleted only when that key is read again, or by an alarm sweep that runs once every 24 h.
